permit.applies: The worker applies; the employer (a promoter, producer or production company) completes the Employer Supplementary Form of INZ 1187.
permit.first: An offer of entertainment work and a written employment agreement, with the employer's guarantee of accommodation, living costs and the return home, and its reasons for not hiring a New Zealander.

fees.what: Visa application (lowest, varies by country of application)

validity.note: 'With this visa you can stay in New Zealand for the time needed to do the work': read as the engagement's own term.

permit.union: Before we make a decision about your application, we ask the New Zealand entertainment industry organisation relevant to your role, if they will support your application to work in New Zealand. Skipped for work of 14 days or less, a certified official co-production, or an accredited employer.
permit.eligibility: you want to work on a film, video or production in New Zealand and you have specific skills that cannot be met by New Zealand's entertainment industry

sources.title: Immigration New Zealand, Entertainers Work Visa
sources.said: Apply for this visa if you want to work on a film, video or production in New Zealand and you have specific skills that cannot be met by New Zealand's entertainment industry. … NZD $1455 … 80% within … 2 weeks … With this visa you can stay in New Zealand for the time needed to do the work. … Your employer must complete a Supplementary Form … a guarantee that they will cover the costs of your accommodation, living expenses and return home … their reasons for not hiring a New Zealander to do the work, and evidence to support those reasons. … Before we make a decision about your application, we ask the New Zealand entertainment industry organisation relevant to your role, if they will support your application to work in New Zealand. … in New Zealand for 14 days or less … on an official co-production that’s been certified by the New Zealand Film Commission … for an entertainment industry accredited company. … If you think your visa may expire before your work is complete, you may apply for another work visa while in New Zealand. … We cannot display any process or costs information until you have provided your country details.

blockers.sought: Any minimum pay or market-rate rule for the Entertainers Work Visa

tried.institution: immigration.govt.nz Entertainers Work Visa page, read whole: names no pay rule, only the employer's guarantee of living costs.
tried.official-register: The Immigration (Visa, Entry Permission, and Related Matters) Regulations and the Operational Manual were not read in this pass.
tried.web-search: Not run separately; the visa page is explicit on its requirements.
tried.archive: Not needed; the live page answered.

note: Immigration New Zealand shows the fee as 'From NZD $1455'; the exact fee is shown only once an applicant's country is entered (the page says it 'cannot display any process or costs information until you have provided your country details'), so only the lowest is held. The visa runs as long as the work needs, so validity has no fixed number. Screenwriters and directors take the same visa (entertainment industry personnel). Those on a short entertainment act or a festival may come on a visitor visa instead (Short Term Entertainment Act Visitor Visa; Arts and Music Festival Visitor Visa), which is not a permit-free engagement and is not modelled as one.
